analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md changed: one bullet added at head line ~110 under 'Unreleased — account erasure' (patch hunk @@ -107,6 +107,7 @@). It describes behavior implemented in code that was NOT supplied, so no code-level security conclusion is possible. Claims the next pass should check against the code:
(1) Cancel restores API keys and provider tokens revoked at confirm, and keys revoked before the confirm stay revoked. Verify that restore targets only rows revoked by that confirm, using a marker or timestamp. A cancel must not resurrect independently revoked credentials (T-004, T-024, T-059).
(2) Scrub adds a privy_user outbox row (schema v33) and clears API key model lists, App Attest shadow events and revocation reasons, rejected-request model names and parameters, Stripe withdrawal failure reasons, payment tx hashes and memos, provider model prices, and the request wallet hash. Verify that the migration is applied, and that the App Attest revocation-reason clearing does not weaken A-015/A-017 revocation fencing or T-053/T-054 revocation semantics.
(3) Late App Attest shadow events from an erased account are refused. Confirm this refusal cannot affect serving authorization (TB-011, A-016).
(4) MicroMDM device removal stays a manual runbook step. This is a residual gap in T-059 (account erasure leaves personal data behind) and should be reflected in the threat model. No concrete regression is demonstrable from this diff.
Threat-model note: the T-059 mitigation text may need updating for the new scrub coverage, the Privy deletion outbox and the cancel-restore semantics. Coverage limit: no source files were supplied, so these are unverified.
